title: [R3-6b] Reach COMPLETE supersession disposition coverage through production writers (DoD 2+5 carved from task-7eddd612)
description:
SPLIT from task-7eddd612 ([R3-6] Gate graph.supersede on COMPLETE disposition coverage), which delivered DoD 1, 3 and 4 with full proof and sat blocked at its plan's intended terminal on DoD 2 and 5. This row carries ONLY the unreachable half so the delivered half can be graded and land.

FILED IN BACKLOG DELIBERATELY: its three prerequisites are all unresolved production constraints, so it must not enter the claim queue yet. Promote it only when a governor or human has ruled on the design question in constraint (2)/(3) below.

WHAT ALREADY SHIPPED IN THE PARENT — do not rebuild it. Committed at cbd717aa (verified an ancestor of HEAD), exactly its 8 owned paths, +290/-7: durable fold-readable coverage; GRAPH_SUPERSEDE_PREPARATION_EXPIRED computed off the command's own decidedAt (Date.now = 0); refusal codes 15 -> 17 pinned by BOTH count and name. Verification leg EXIT 0, Tests 164 passed (164). Six mutants drilled, all six RED, restores SHA256-proved. Parent evidence: comment-64f70c4b055941ff815999d2a289de30 and comment-93187ecc2bde4797b8a62d74361c474b.

WHAT THIS ROW OWES: the parent's DoD 2 and DoD 5 — COMPLETE disposition coverage reached through PRODUCTION writers, not fixtures. The parent measured it unreachable at HEAD and named THREE constraints, each blocking on its own. The parent's measurement is the starting point, not a claim to trust — re-measure each at your own HEAD:

1. apps/daemon/src/scheduler/supersession-dispositions.ts:73-80 requires all six disposition kinds, and :64 rejects duplicates.
2. apps/daemon/src/planning/supersession-preparation-history.ts:119-130 `lineageFactsFor` HARDCODES "ADD". Combined with (1) that is a proof, not a gap: one lineage misses five kinds, two or more duplicate ADD. No count can reach built.ok.
3. apps/daemon/src/planning/journey-authority-bodies.ts:158-161 throws on a second node id, and CARRY has no durable evidence reader.
Consequently apps/daemon/src/planning/lineages.ts:63-69 always answers PARTIAL, pinned at service.test.ts:308.

CARRY-FORWARD RULING, binding here (governor, comment-6a8d5bd8 on the parent): COMPLETE disposition coverage is PER-LINEAGE, measured at supersede time from predecessor + successor node-authority hashes. The kernel does not loosen. CARRY STAYS UNEMITTABLE — an unchanged node is REQUALIFY, and CARRY needs evaluateCarryForward's seven durable readers, none of which exist. If this row starts to look like a place to assert carry authority, STOP: that is task-08efb6f0's surface and a security boundary.

DO NOT relax the six-kind requirement, the duplicate rejection, or the PARTIAL answer to make a suite green. Those three are the guarantee; the work is to make production genuinely able to emit COMPLETE coverage, or to prove it cannot and escalate the design.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK first, reporting blocked and naming the failing constraint rather than proceeding: re-measure all three constraints at your own HEAD, each grep UNPIPED with its own exit code and paired with a positive control (`git grep -c export HEAD -- <same file>` exiting 0). Record `git rev-parse HEAD` and quote it. Confirm supersession-dispositions.ts still requires six kinds and rejects duplicates, supersession-preparation-history.ts lineageFactsFor still hardcodes ADD, and journey-authority-bodies.ts still throws on a second node id.

A PRODUCTION writer path emits disposition facts for more than one lineage and for more than the ADD kind, with no fixture standing in for a writer. `lineageFactsFor` derives its kind from durable state rather than a hardcoded literal, and journey-authority-bodies accepts the node ids a real multi-node supersession presents.

With those writers reachable, a real supersession over a multi-node lineage reaches COMPLETE coverage through the production fold, and the PARTIAL answer at lineages.ts:63-69 is returned only when coverage genuinely is partial. The arm pinned at service.test.ts:308 is updated to assert the discriminating case, never deleted.

The six-kind requirement and the duplicate rejection at supersession-dispositions.ts:64/:73-80 are UNCHANGED, and CARRY remains unemittable per the standing ruling. A mutation removing either fence, or emitting CARRY, reds a named arm.

Mutation drills prove each new writer path is load-bearing: reverting lineageFactsFor to a hardcoded ADD reds the multi-kind arm, and restoring the second-node-id throw reds the multi-lineage arm. Restores proven by `git diff --exit-code` for tracked paths and SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup for untracked ones, in a call separate from the restore.

Gates standalone, foreground, unpiped, exit 0 with nonzero counts quoted: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` (quote the `$ tsc` echo) and the focused daemon suites covering dispositions, lineages and supersession preparation. Commit by explicit pathspec; the parent's eight owned paths are NOT re-committed by this row.
taskRails: Do not rebuild or re-commit anything task-7eddd612 delivered at cbd717aa. That slice is verified good; this row is additive.
Do not relax the six-kind requirement, the duplicate rejection, or the PARTIAL fallback to turn a suite green. Those are the guarantee this row exists to satisfy honestly.
CARRY stays unemittable. A disposition record is not a place to assert carry authority — that is task-08efb6f0's surface and a security boundary. Stop and report if the design drifts there.

If the three constraints prove unresolvable without a design change, report blocked with the measurement rather than narrowing this row's DoD. A second permanently-blocked row is worse than an honest design escalation.

Ruling clause 4 requires this code to exist: "A completeness fact that can never refuse is worthless; the whole point of moving the measurement is that it can now refuse for a REAL reason instead of an unreachable one." (2) THE COMPLETE ARM (graph-supersede-service.test.ts): a real multi-lineage supersession whose predecessor and successor authority hashes ARE derivable reaches COMPLETE coverage through the production fold.
(3) THE DISCRIMINATING PARTIAL ARM (supersession-preparation-service.test.ts): coverage answers PARTIAL only when it genuinely is partial. (4) CARRY REMAINS UNEMITTABLE (ruling clause 3, taskRail 3): an unchanged node is REQUALIFY. Its own note says "COMPLETE. Deliberately not wired yet — `lineageFactsFor` hardcodes ADD, so the scheduler set…". That containment is why this is a correction of WHERE the property is measured rather than a relaxation of the standard.

DoD 2 as filed asked to derive its kind from durable state; the amendment (comment-47283bd9) reverses that, because at prepare time no successor exists and deriving anything else would fabricate one. IF REMOVING THE PREPARATION'S CALL LEAVES `buildSupersessionDispositions` WITH NO PRODUCTION CONSUMER, do not delete it and do not invent a caller — record the fact and name it for a follow-up. Deleting a scheduler fence to tidy an orphan is precisely what taskRail 2 forbids, and a fabricated caller is worse.

comments.content:
ARCHITECT REVIEW OF THE PARK — IT IS CORRECT, AND HERE IS THE EXACT RULING STILL OWED. architect-a69740e0, 2026-08-28, measured at HEAD 0bf353ff. I considered promoting this row to PLANNING and decided against it on measurement. Recording that so the next reader inherits the answer instead of re-deriving it.

=== WHY I LOOKED ===
This row sits in BACKLOG, which no agent role can claim, and its filing says: "Promote it only when a governor or human has ruled on the design question in constraint (2)/(3)." The governor's CARRY ruling (comment-6a8d5bd8 on the parent) already exists and is cited in the description, so the question was whether that ruling discharges the gate. It does not — it settles one half and leaves the other genuinely open.

=== WHAT THE CARRY RULING DOES SETTLE ===
It defines COMPLETE as PER-LINEAGE completeness measured at supersede time from predecessor + successor node-authority hashes, and it settles that CARRY STAYS UNEMITTABLE (an unchanged node is REQUALIFY; CARRY needs evaluateCarryForward's seven durable readers, none of which exist — that surface belongs to task-08efb6f0). Constraint (2)'s "derive the kind from durable state rather than a hardcoded literal" follows directly from it: the ruling names the predecessor/successor hash pair as the source, so un-hardcoding `kind: "ADD"` is ordinary engineering, not a design question.
Measured at HEAD, that constraint still holds: `supersession-preparation-history.ts:126-137` `lineageFactsFor` maps every lineage to a literal `kind: "ADD"` (:131), through an `as unknown as SupersessionNodeFacts` cast at :136.

=== WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, AND WHY THIS IS NOT ORDINARY ENGINEERING ===
Constraint (3) is a DELIBERATE FAIL-CLOSED AUTHORITY FENCE with its reasoning written into the code, not an incidental single-node limit. `journey-authority-bodies.ts` `graphContentOf` states it verbatim:
  "The journey's graph: ONE execution-bearing node, zero edges, keyed by the journey's own node, so two journeys naming different nodes seal different graphs rather than colliding on one content-addressed body row."
  "Fail CLOSED rather than silently dropping: the snapshot is single-node by design, so a caller passing two would seal a plan naming both against a graph that contains one of them."
  `if (nodeKey === undefined || extra.length > 0) throw new Error(...)`
So the throw exists to prevent a SEALED PLAN NAMING NODES ITS GRAPH DOES NOT CONTAIN, and to keep two journeys from colliding on one content-addressed body row. DoD-2 of this row asks for "journey-authority-bodies accepts the node ids a real multi-node graph produces" — that is a request to remove that fence. Removing it changes what a sealed journey graph MEANS and reopens both hazards the comment names. An agent may implement a multi-node producer; an agent may not decide that a fail-closed integrity fence should come down. That is the same shape as the (a)/(b) ruling the human took on the parent, and it is why this row's filing demanded a ruling in the first place.

=== THE QUESTION, PUT PRECISELY SO IT CAN BE ANSWERED IN ONE LINE ===
May the journey graph producer emit MULTI-NODE graphs — i.e. may `graphContentOf`'s single-node throw be replaced by a real multi-node snapshot — and if so, what replaces the two guarantees its comment currently provides: (i) that a sealed plan never names a node its graph lacks, and (ii) that two journeys naming different nodes cannot collide on one content-addressed body row?
Until that is answered, DoD-2 and DoD-3 are unreachable by construction, exactly as the parent measured. The parent task-7eddd612 is DONE at 8/8 with its delivered half graded, so nothing is waiting on this row for grading.

=== WHAT I DID NOT DO, DELIBERATELY ===
I did not promote it, and I did not narrow the DoD to the half that IS reachable (constraint 2 alone). Landing a kind-deriving `lineageFactsFor` while the producer stays single-node would still never reach COMPLETE — one lineage cannot cover six kinds — so a partial promotion buys a commit and no capability, and it would make the row look addressed while its actual blocker stands. If a governor or human rules the fence may come down, this becomes a normal plannable row and I will take it.

comments.content:
DoD 2 AMENDMENT + PATH CORRECTIONS. architect-fdbab575, 2026-08-29, measured at HEAD 62b4d7f6. This comment is the amendment surface; DoD items are not editable by any architect tool, so grade DoD 2 against the text below.

=== FIRST, TWO OF THE THREE NAMED PATHS DO NOT EXIST. Re-measure before believing any line number. ===
  `apps/daemon/src/scheduler/supersession-dispositions.ts` — NO SUCH FILE. The six-kind demand and the duplicate rejection live in **packages/scheduler/src/supersession/supersession-dispositions.ts**, at :65 (`new Set(kinds).size !== kinds.length || new Set(keys).size !== keys.length`) and :78 (`SUPERSESSION_DISPOSITION_KINDS.some((kind) => !present.has(kind))`).
  `apps/daemon/src/planning/lineages.ts` — NO SUCH FILE. The always-PARTIAL answer is **apps/daemon/src/planning/supersession-preparation-lineages.ts**, :64 `if (built.ok) return { coverage: "COMPLETE", digest: built.digest };` / :69 `return { coverage: "PARTIAL", digest: digestOf("lineages", lineages) };`, fed by :63 `buildSupersessionDispositions(lineageFactsFor(lineages))`.
  `journey-authority-bodies.ts` IS correct, but the throw is at :157-161, not :158-161.

=== DoD 4 IS CONSISTENT WITH THE RULING. I checked this first because it looked like a contradiction and it is not. ===
DoD 4 keeps the six-kind requirement and the duplicate rejection UNCHANGED; governor-fd35a081's ruling (comment-6a8d5bd8) retires "the PREPARATION's six-kind coverage fact". Those are different things and both hold: the FENCE stays where it is, in the scheduler builder, and what changes is that the PREPARATION stops using it as a coverage oracle. graph-supersede-dispositions.ts's own header states the split — `buildSupersessionDispositions` "is used by the preparation for its coverage fact", while "the KERNEL asks only for a non-empty set of uniquely keyed, well-shaped entries." Nothing in this row removes a fence, so DoD 4's mutation arms stand as written.

=== DoD 2 DOES CONFLICT WITH THE RULING, AND THE RULING WINS ===
DoD 2 as filed requires: "`lineageFactsFor` derives its kind from durable state rather than a hardcoded literal, and journey-authority-bodies accepts the node ids a real multi-node supersession presents."
The ruling explains why the hardcode is CORRECT, not a defect: "COMPLETE means PER-LINEAGE completeness, measured at SUPERSEDE time from predecessor + successor node-authority hashes. That is a correction of WHERE the property is measured, not a relaxation of the standard: **at prepare time the successor does not exist, which is exactly why lineageFactsFor has to hardcode ADD**."
So making `lineageFactsFor` derive a kind at PREPARE time would require inventing a successor that does not yet exist — fabricated authority, and epic rail 4 forbids it. Widening `journey-authority-bodies` to accept multiple node ids to feed that derivation is the same error one layer down: the header at :154-156 records the single-node graph as a deliberate content-identity property, not a limitation ("two journeys naming different nodes seal different graphs rather than colliding on one content-addressed body row").

DoD 2, AS IT NOW READS:
"A PRODUCTION path emits per-lineage disposition facts derived at SUPERSEDE time from predecessor + successor node-authority hashes, with no fixture standing in for a writer. The coverage fact moves OFF the prepare-time six-kind oracle and onto that per-lineage derivation. `lineageFactsFor` KEEPS its ADD literal — at prepare time no successor exists, so ADD is the only honest answer and deriving anything else would fabricate one — and `journey-authority-bodies`' single-node-id throw at :157-161 is UNCHANGED, being a content-identity property rather than a limitation. Both hashes come from `GraphRevisionContent.nodeAuthority`, which `encodeGraphContent` already embeds in the content identity, so a disposition can still only cite authority the content hash covers."

=== WHERE THE WIRING POINT ALREADY IS, so this is smaller than the DoD implies ===
The per-lineage derivation is ALREADY BUILT: `apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-supersede-dispositions.ts` derives kinds from predecessor/successor hashes (:50 shows the ADD arm with `predecessorAuthorityHash: null`). And `apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-supersede-facts.ts:178` carries the reserved slot with its own note: "COMPLETE. Deliberately not wired yet — `lineageFactsFor` hardcodes ADD, so the scheduler set...". This row wires that slot to the supersede-time derivation and moves supersession-preparation-lineages.ts off the impossible oracle. It does not build a new derivation.

=== RULING CLAUSES 4 AND 5 ARE THE ACCEPTANCE BAR, not an afterthought ===
"COVERAGE MUST STILL BE ABLE TO FAIL. Keep a pinned refusal code for a lineage whose disposition cannot be derived from predecessor + successor content. A completeness fact that can never refuse is worthless." And: "DRILL THE REFUSAL, not just the pass.
